questions.prompt: What can QoS do on a busy link?

options: 150 ms
15 seconds
1 ms

The total bandwidth of a busy link

options: In the DNS record

In the IP header
In the TCP header

options: 0 (best effort)

Bulk traffic that can wait

Holds it in a buffer to send later

options: WRED
FIFO
Shaping

First in, first out, with no priorities
The highest priority queue always goes first

Every queue is the same size
Voice is sent last of all

Its own physical interface
A separate routing table
A guaranteed share of the link

questions.prompt: What does LLQ add to CBWFQ?

A capped priority queue for voice
A label on every packet in the core

questions.prompt: In MPLS, what do core routers look at to forward a packet?
options: The DNS name
The label
The MAC address
The full IP address

options: The P (provider core)
The DNS resolver router
The CE (customer edge)
The PE (provider edge)

questions.prompt: Which protocol do MPLS routers use to agree on labels?
options: STP
BGP
DTP
LDP

A label that marks voice traffic as EF

questions.prompt: What is tail drop?

questions.prompt: What is TCP global synchronization?

questions.prompt: How does RED help?
options: It adds bandwidth when the link is busy
It drops a few packets early, at random
It moves voice into the priority queue
It drops every packet once the queue fills

questions.prompt: How is WRED different from RED?
options: It marks packets instead of dropping them
It has different thresholds per DSCP
It only ever drops voice traffic early
It needs no queue at all to work

questions.prompt: What does ECN do instead of dropping packets?
options: Changes their DSCP to best effort
Sends them down a second link
Holds them until the queue empties
Marks them to signal congestion

questions.prompt: Why should you never use RED on voice?
options: Voice doesn't back off; it just breaks
RED only works on UDP traffic flows
Voice has no DSCP mark at all
Voice packets are much too small to drop

questions.prompt: Why load-balance per flow rather than per packet?
options: So one flow's packets stay in order
